Maria Chen: Quick heads-up — Hildebrand is scheduled for dedicated pool go‑live next Thu. Customer expects steady 180 rps, peak ~700 rps. They committed 4xA100-equivalent but want aggressive autoscaling. We need a concrete quota plan, warmup schedule, and a short smoke/load test runbook. I also flagged renewal risk: they're on a 6‑month commit and will revisit if initial performance/costs look off.
Aj Patel: On it. I'll own the load probe and priming. Proposed plan: staged shadow traffic across 3 windows (10%, 40%, 100%) over 2 days, then a 1‑hour soak at 70% of expected peak.
Samir Rao: For model variants — recommend primary = redwood/opt-8-qa, fallback = opt-6-q8 (quantized). We'll start with 16‑token KV cache priming to reduce cold token latency. If latency at 70% peak > 180ms p50 we fallback to quantized variant.
Lucy Park: KMS + VPC checks are green for their account. Need confirmation on egress IP allowlist from Hildebrand and ensure NAT gateway throughput is accounted for. Also: who's owning the canary rollback policy?
Maria Chen: @Aj Patel take rollback policy (canary 5% for 15m with auto-failover to hosted). @Samir Rao will push the fallback artifact and post model hash. I'll loop in AE re: renewal talking points.
Aj Patel: Drafting load script now. Example k6 run command we plan to use for the soak:
```
k6 run --vus 300 --duration 60m --out json=hildebrand_soak.json hildebrand_probe.js
```
Script will hit the /v1/generate endpoint with a small prompt set (10 prompts) and record token counts. We'll also run a quick prefix-prime step:
```
# prefix prime (single-shot requests to warm KV cache)
for i in $(seq 1 500); do curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.com/v1/generate -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" -d '{"model":"redwood/opt-8-qa","prompt":"warmup"}'; done
```
Samir Rao: I'll publish the quantized fallback build to the dedicated model catalog and attach model hash here when ready. Also recommending autoscale thresholds: GPU utilization target 65% (scale up at 75%), token backlog threshold 4000, and request latency threshold p95 800ms to trigger scale-up.
Lucy Park: Noted. For warmup windows, we should schedule them during customer business hours in their primary region (us-east-1). Also will add a short run to validate KMS sign/verify latency under load.
Maria Chen: Action list: 1) Aj — run prefix prime + staged soak (ETA Wed EOD) 2) Samir — push fallback and post model hash (ETA Tue) 3) Lucy — confirm egress IPs + KMS soak (ETA Wed morning) 4) Maria — prep renewal talking points and cost sensitivity notes (ETA Wed noon).
Aj Patel: I'll upload the k6 outputs to the shared folder and tag the thread. Expect initial smoke by Wed 18:00 UTC.
Samir Rao: Model hash: sha256:9f3b7a2e4d1c... (pushed to dedicated catalog). Fallback tested locally with 30% quantization and 5% quality regress — acceptable per their SLO.
Lucy Park: Egress list requested from Hildebrand — waiting on the customer's network team. KMS latency baseline (single key sign) ~12ms. Under 70% soak we'll retest.
Maria Chen: FYI AE asked for cost delta estimate between primary vs fallback — Samir can you give a % token-cost delta after your tests?
Samir Rao: Estimated token cost reduction ~28% with quantized fallback at similar latency in our bench. Will provide final numbers post-soak.
capacity-bot: Reminder set — capacity-probe run scheduled Wed 18:00 UTC. Use /ops status once runs complete. :spiral_calendar: 
Aj Patel: Quick note — will include a short failure-injection step (nuke one GPU in the pool) to validate routing/fallback. Low blast radius.
Maria Chen: Thank you all — please post results in this thread. I'll summarize for the AE and include renewal risk mitigation steps (cost levers, shorter canary, usage-based phase). :thumbsup:
